reports.title: Quarter of 2026; Raises Outlook for the Year

desk.headline: Revenue up 42% to $314.1m, beat; full-year outlook raised and Q4 guidance set
results: Revenue rose 42% to $314.1m, slightly ahead of the $312.6m estimate; merchandise volume (GMV) grew 35% to $2.04bn.
Fulfilment revenue jumped 54% to $180.1m and service fees rose about 30% to $134.0m; the acquired Passport business added to both.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 54% to $63.7m and the margin widened by about 1.6 points to 20.3%, though gross margin slipped to 44.8%.
GAAP profit of $81.1m ($0.47 a share) was lifted by a $49.0m one-off tax benefit; adjusted profit was $63.0m ($0.37 a share).
Free cash flow was $66.4m; the company bought back $53m of shares, leaving $447m under its $500m plan.

guidance.summary: Global-e again raised its 2026 targets, lifting the low end of all three ranges, and gave its first Q4 outlook of $464–488m in revenue. The top of the revenue range edged down slightly as the range was tightened.

points: Same-store sales stayed solid but slowed from the first half, and the Q4 range allows for that; the CFO said the main holiday peak is still ahead.
Shopify Managed Markets volumes picked up through the quarter; merchants using the new guaranteed-shipping pricing saw conversion rise about 50%.
Passport's first integration phase is done and it remains on track for its 2026 targets, with margin and cash flow gains expected in 2027.
Service-fee take rates are expected to hold fairly steady; Passport's lower margins and paused fuel surcharges weighed on gross margin.
No formal 2027 guidance, but management expects another year of strong growth and profitability, and will keep buying back shares.
